title: GNN-assisted Back-side Clock Routing Methodology for Advance Technologies
problem: Clock routing traditionally relies on front-side metal layers which exhibit higher parasitics. Advanced technologies like 3nm provide back-side metal layers with substantially lower parasitics that remain underutilized for clock distribution.
motivation: Back-side metal layers in advanced technologies offer lower parasitics, enabling improved clock-tree distribution that can significantly increase effective frequency while maintaining equivalent power consumption.
method: A Graph Neural Network-based framework optimally distributes clock-trees between front-side and back-side metal layers. Back-side buffers are integrated to enable clock-net creation on the back-side, with the GNN framework considering parasitic characteristics and shared power delivery network constraints for joint optimization across both layers.
key_novelty: Using GNN to intelligently partition and route clock trees across front-side and back-side metal layers, exploiting the lower parasitics of back-side layers in advanced nodes.
contributions: GNN-based framework for optimized clock-tree distribution across front and back metal layers
Methodology for enabling back-side clock nets with buffer placement strategy
Demonstration of up to 13% effective frequency improvement at 3nm with equivalent power consumption
Integration of back-side clock routing with shared power delivery network
limitations: Applicability beyond 3nm, scalability to different power delivery network topologies, and comparison against other advanced routing methodologies are not discussed.
primary_theme: GNN-optimized back-side clock routing for advanced technologies
